trend.title: Wells Fargo and Bank of America CRE Write-Offs Jump to $107M and $105M in Q3 as Problem Loans Shrink
trend.scope: U.S. money-center bank commercial real estate loan books (third-quarter 2026 earnings, Wells Fargo and Bank of America)
trend.metric: CRE write-offs: Wells Fargo $107M (from $16M), Bank of America $105M (from $2M); problem CRE loans down 20% and 17%
trend.summary: Third-quarter results show the two banks taking far larger commercial real estate losses while shrinking their troubled books. Wells Fargo's CRE write-offs rose to $107M from $16M in the second quarter, its problem CRE loans fell 20% to $2.7B, and its office loans fell 7% to $18.6B. Bank of America's CRE write-offs rose to $105M from $2M while troubled CRE loans fell 17% to $888M. Both cut reserves: Wells Fargo to about $1.61 per $100 of CRE loans from $1.77, and Bank of America to $1.14 from $1.28.
trend.significance: Rising write-offs alongside falling problem-loan balances mean banks are resolving distressed CRE credits rather than extending them: note sales, discounted payoffs, foreclosures and receiverships. Borrowers on maturing bank loans should expect less forbearance and faster enforcement, guarantors should expect deficiency and guaranty claims to follow sales at a loss, and buyers of discounted notes step into the lender's enforcement rights, which tends to bring more litigation, not less.
